Title: Document 10
Content: Source: Anna R., `14text(-year-old)` member of a kulak family, interviewed in `text(1993)` for Memories of the Dispossessed, published `text(1998)`.

In `text(1928)`, I just started to notice people disappearing: `text(first one)`, then another, and another. My parents didn't join the commune, remaining independent farmers. `text(First)` they had a massive tax to pay; it was so high they were quite unable to pay it. After that, activists from the commune descended on us, breaking all the locks on the barns and clearing us out of all our corn. Next time they came to inventory our property. They noted it all down and carried it off. We were woken up in the night in early spring, `text(1929)`; we were told, 'You're going for good.' At dawn they lined several families up in the Rural Council building and then sent us off into the unknown.
